# Example Output — Cloudflare R2 Static Data

*Generated by applying the Cloudflare R2 Static Data skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. Key layout

```text
streets/v1/<state>/<street-id>.json     # shards
streets/v1/meta.json                    # manifest — written last
```

- **Version in the key.** `v1` is the first versioned build. The quarterly revision becomes `streets/v2/...`; nothing under `v1` is ever overwritten, which is what makes immutable caching safe.
- **Prefixes the app reads:** `act`, `nsw`, `nt`, `qld`, `sa`, `tas`, `vic`, `wa` — all eight, listed in `prefixes.txt` for the release gate.
- **Version selection:** the release config holds `STREETS_VERSION=v1`. The app builds URLs from it and reads `meta.json` only for the build date — the manifest no longer decides whether the data is there.

## 2. Bucket and access

| Item | Setting |
|---|---|
| Public access | Custom domain `data.<your-domain>` connected to `<bucket>` (zone on the same account) |
| `r2.dev` | Disabled — it is rate-limited and not for production |
| Upload token | S3 API token, **Object Read & Write**, applied to `<bucket>` only. The account-level token is revoked |
| CLI | Profile `r2`, region `auto`, endpoint `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` |
| Edge cache | Cache Rule on `data.<your-domain>` marking requests eligible for cache — JSON is not cached at the edge by default |
| Browser access | Bucket CORS allows `GET` from the app's origin; the site's CSP `connect-src` gains `https://data.<your-domain>` |

## 3. Upload plan

One sync per state, eight running in parallel — never two on the same prefix:

```bash
aws s3 sync "out/streets/v1/$state/" "s3://<bucket>/streets/v1/$state/" \
  --profile r2 --endpoint-url "$R2" \
  --content-type application/json \
  --cache-control "public, max-age=2592000, immutable" \
  --only-show-errors
```

- Replaces the per-file `aws s3 cp` loop that was estimating about 30 hours; the full 1.19 million shards now upload in an evening.
- Every object gets the same `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control`; nothing is uploaded without them.
- `meta.json` is **not** part of these syncs.

## 4. Release gate

Run after the syncs, before `meta.json` and before the release switches:

| Prefix | Built | On bucket (first run) | On bucket (after re-sync) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `act` | 6,214 | 6,214 | 6,214 |
| `nsw` | 384,102 | 384,102 | 384,102 |
| `nt` | 4,905 | 4,905 | 4,905 |
| `qld` | 248,530 | 248,530 | 248,530 |
| `sa` | 88,953 | 88,953 | 88,953 |
| `tas` | 31,240 | 31,240 | 31,240 |
| `vic` | 301,877 | **287,410 — INCOMPLETE** | 301,877 |
| `wa` | 121,406 | 121,406 | 121,406 |

- First run failed on `vic` (the laptop slept mid-sync). Only `vic` was re-synced; the second run passed. Under the old process this was the 13-minute 404 incident — this time it never reached users.
- Then, in order: upload `streets/v1/meta.json` → set `STREETS_VERSION=v1` → deploy.

## 5. Verification

```text
curl -sI https://data.<your-domain>/streets/v1/vic/<street-id>.json
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/json
cache-control: public, max-age=2592000, immutable
cf-cache-status: HIT            (second request)
```

- One sample key from each of the eight prefixes returns 200 with these headers.
- The `r2.dev` URL now refuses requests, confirming nothing still depends on it.
- Next quarter: build `streets/v2/`, pass the same gate, switch `STREETS_VERSION`, and keep `v1` until no deployed release reads it.
